summary_en: This study tests belumosudil, an oral selective inhibitor of ROCK2, to help prevent graft-versus-host disease in people with blood cancer who have had a stem cell transplant. The drug is taken by mouth (oral), and the dose, how often it is taken, and how long it is given are not stated. This is a Phase II study; its main outcome is not stated, but it aims to find out whether adding belumosudil may be an effective prevention approach and to look at safety.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa belumosudil, un inhibidor selectivo de ROCK2 que se toma por vía oral, para ayudar a prevenir la enfermedad de injerto contra huésped en personas con cáncer de la sangre que recibieron un trasplante de células madre. El medicamento se toma por vía oral; la dosis, la frecuencia y la duración del tratamiento no se indican. Es un estudio de fase II; el resultado principal no se indica, pero busca saber si agregar belumosudil puede ser un enfoque eficaz para prevenir la enfermedad de injerto contra huésped y evaluar su seguridad.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with a blood cancer in morphologic remission.
Received a stem cell transplant from a 7-8/8 matched related or unrelated donor, or a haploidentical donor.
Stem cell graft taken from peripheral blood.
Transplant timing limits apply at consent and before starting belumosudil.
Karnofsky score at least 70%, with adequate liver and kidney function tests.
not_for: Received a CD34+ selected or engineered stem cell graft.
Received in vivo T cell depletion, such as anti-thymocyte globulin.
Uncontrolled heart conditions, heart failure, or heart attack within the past 6 months.
Active secondary cancer, or prior cancer needing systemic therapy within 5 years (with listed exceptions).
Active GVHD needing systemic therapy, prior belumosudil use, or allergy to belumosudil or other ROCK2 inhibitors.
